messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: dynamically sized data structures?
parts:
Hi!

I am trying to simulate a repeated event counting model. So I have J subjects (fixed) and for each subject a censoring time C_j. The issue I run into when simulating this is that the number of events per subject is a random number such that I need a dynamically sized data structure for this (I have to record the time-points when an event occurs).

Any idea on this?

The brute force solution would be to pre-allocate a data-structure with a fixed maximal number of events, but this feels bad...

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] dynamically sized data structures?
parts:
If the simulation is a pure simulation in generated quantities,
then there's no problem --- use a local variable. There's no
way to output variable-sized structures --- it would break all of
our posterior reporting.

I'm also afraid there is no good way to convert real values
to integers. That's by design, because it loses derivative
information.

You could preallocate and use a while loop to hack around
this restriction. I'm waiting for someone to write the master
hack function that uses binary search and while loops to make
it at least O(log n) instead of O(n), but I'm not going to be
the one to do it :-)

- Bob

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] dynamically sized data structures?
parts:
Hi Bob!

Ok, so here we go as I needed it myself. Below is a version of findInterval in R. The _slow version is what I used so far. One question: Is it possible to get rid of the nasty warning about the integer arithmetic, i.e. I would prefer to call a int floor(int) function instead, but Stan does not has this function.

  /* find_interval, see findInterval from R
   * i.e. find the ranks of x in sorted; sorted is assumed to be weakly-sorted.
   */
  int[] find_interval_slow(vector x, vector sorted) {
    int res[num_elements(x)];
    // very brutal and ineffcient way of doing this, but well, it's
    // C++ speed...
    for(i in 1:num_elements(x)) {
      res[i] <- rank(append_row(rep_vector(x[i], 1), sorted), 1);
    }
    return(res);
  }
  /* faster version which uses bisectioning search
   */
  int find_interval_elem(real x, vector sorted) {
    int res;
    int N;
    int max_iter;
    real left;
    real right;
    int left_ind;
    int right_ind;
    int iter;
   
    N <- num_elements(sorted);
    max_iter <- N;
    left  <- sorted[1] - x;
    right <- sorted[N] - x;
    if(0 < left) return(0);
    if(0 > right) return(N);
    iter <- 1;
    left_ind  <- 1;
    right_ind <- N;
    while((right_ind - left_ind) > 1  && iter != max_iter) {
      int mid_ind;
      real mid;
      // is there a controlled way without being yelled at with a
      // warning?
      mid_ind <- (left_ind + right_ind) / 2;
      mid <- sorted[mid_ind] - x;
      if (left * mid  < 0) { right <- mid; right_ind <- mid_ind; }
      if (right * mid < 0) { left  <- mid; left_ind  <- mid_ind; }
      iter <- iter + 1;
    }
    if(iter == max_iter)
      print("Maximum number of iterations reached.");
    return(left_ind);
  }
 
  int[] find_interval(vector x, vector sorted) {
    int res[num_elements(x)];
    for(i in 1:num_elements(x)) {
      res[i] <- find_interval_elem(x[i], sorted);
    }
    return(res);
  }



Cheers,
Sebastian

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] dynamically sized data structures?
parts:
Isn't

int floor(int);

just the identity function? We are intentionally avoiding

int floor(real);

And no, no way to do integer division without a warning.

I suppose we can add another item to our to-do list to
provide some kind of guidance to turn off compiler warnings.
Too many false positives are bad news. I added it to our
longer-term to-do list pending a spec and time to work on it.

- Bob

parts:
Hi Bob!

Yes, you are right int floor(int) is not what I meant. I used integers to evaluate an expression which implictly gets casted to a real, so I needed a int floor(real).

Thanks for adding a note to the todo. Making Stan more silent via options would be very welcome.

One more warning if anyone picks up the function: Use with care wrt to what is data and what not, safest is to only use the function in transformed data - or you will ruin the performance of any Stan program.

@Bob: Is such a function of interest to the general community, i.e. the find_interval above is similar to the rank function (at the additional expense of needing a sorted vector), but performs much faster from my tests. If yes, I am happy to open an issue with a slightly corrected version of the above.

Best,
Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] dynamically sized data structures?
parts:
Well, we didn't include a built-in int floor(double) on purpose.

It would be OK in transformed data. But we don't have a way
to mark functions as being usable only on data and not on
parameters. I may have to do that at some point. It's one of
the reason the integrate_ode() expressions are defined directly
rather than just being function application (the other being functions
as arguments).

We don't have a good way to release functions to the community
as a whole. Maybe we're going to need something like CRAN
for Stan!

- Bob
